headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: OpenHands can write/egress broadly while Prefect can ingest API data, creating medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can read/write files, run browsers, and use MCP; Prefect can call APIs and orchestrate workflows. The pair has a mounted-volume bridge via OpenHands and no documented provenance or isolation between outputs and inputs, so prompt-like content in shared files or workflow metadata can steer OpenHands. This is not provably blocked.
conditions: IF Prefect writes attacker-controlled text into a shared mounted volume or workflow artifact that OpenHands later reads as instructions
IF OpenHands consumes MCP/file content without provenance filtering
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different volumes
Disable MCP for the OpenHands session
Add a manual review step before OpenHands reads Prefect-produced artifacts
Prefix all Prefect outputs with non-executable metadata headers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and content-type enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenHands touches files mounted into its runtime and handles model-provider API keys; Prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad network egress. If both share a workspace or mounted volume, file contents can flow from OpenHands into Prefect outputs or API calls. The profiles do not show local-only inference or a hard isolation boundary, so leakage is plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mounted workspace or artifact directory
IF Prefect serializes workflow metadata containing file-derived content to external services
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Remove secrets from any shared directory before Prefect runs
Restrict Prefect tasks to metadata-only inputs
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress; Prefect can also perform networked orchestration. If both operate on the same repo or mutable workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can race and corrupt state. The profiles show no locking or coordination primitive, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git checkout or writable directory
IF Prefect triggers actions while OpenHands is editing the same files
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable git mutation in one agent during shared runs
Run one agent read-only until the other finishes
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can generate code, browser-derived findings, and file edits; Prefect can orchestrate downstream workflows. If Prefect treats OpenHands output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into automated pipeline actions. The interaction is plausible but not documented as fully autonomous, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Prefect consumes OpenHands-produced artifacts or summaries without validation
IF Prefect triggers downstream jobs based on those artifacts
mitigations: Require human approval before Prefect acts on OpenHands output
Add schema validation to OpenHands-produced files
Compare outputs against a second source before execution
Limit Prefect to read-only ingestion of OpenHands artifacts
requires-engineering: implement confidence and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: OpenHands handles model-provider API keys and runtime files, while Prefect is documented here as touching workflow metadata only. No explicit residency, retention, or regulated-data mismatch is shown, so compliance risk is limited to documented gaps rather than a clear breach pathway. Prefect is not cited for a stronger claim because its profile lacks such controls.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into OpenHands runtime files and then exported through Prefect-managed workflows
IF the deployment stores workflow metadata in a jurisdiction with stricter residency rules
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Document retention for workflow metadata
Mask secrets before any Prefect export
Review deployment region settings
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
